title: The Overpaid Fare and the Long Drive Back
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] I have been driving a taxi for eleven years now, and most nights blend together into one long, tired blur.
Narrator: But one night last spring still stands out clearly, because of something small that happened right at the very end of a ride.
Narrator: [gently] A young tourist got into my car late at night, exhausted after a long flight, and asked me to take him to his hotel.
Narrator: He didn't speak our language well, and he seemed nervous about handling unfamiliar money, so he simply handed me a folded bundle of cash.
Narrator: [carefully] He said, please just take what I owe you, since I don't fully understand the currency yet after arriving today.
Narrator: I counted it later under a streetlight and realized he had accidentally given me almost four times the actual fare.
Narrator: [reflective] It was already close to midnight, my shift had technically ended, and I was genuinely exhausted after a long, difficult day of driving.
Narrator: Still, I turned my taxi around and drove back toward his hotel, because keeping that money felt like stealing from someone who trusted me completely.
Narrator: [honestly] When I found him in the lobby, he looked confused, and then embarrassed, once I explained his simple counting mistake.
Narrator: He tried to insist I keep the extra money anyway, calling it a generous tip for driving all the way back so late.
Narrator: [warmly] I explained that returning the accidental overpayment was required. If he freely chose a tip after seeing the correct fare, that would be a separate decision.
Narrator: He thanked me and chose a small tip after checking the fare. I accepted it, then drove home relieved that the payment was clear.
Narrator: [sincere] Since that night, I count unfamiliar notes with passengers, point to the meter, and confirm both the fare and any tip before we separate.

quiz.question: How long has the narrator been driving a taxi?
quiz.explanation: He says he has been driving a taxi for eleven years.

quiz.question: Why did the tourist hand him a folded bundle of cash?
options: He wanted to give a huge tip
He didn't fully understand the currency yet
quiz.explanation: The tourist said he didn't fully understand the currency yet, so he asked the driver to take what he owed.

quiz.question: What did the narrator discover when he counted the money later?
options: It was less than the fare
It was almost four times the actual fare
quiz.explanation: He realized the tourist had accidentally given him almost four times the actual fare.

quiz.question: What did the narrator do after discovering the mistake?
options: He turned his taxi around and drove back to the hotel
quiz.explanation: Even though his shift had ended and he was exhausted, he turned his taxi around and drove back.

quiz.question: How did the narrator describe his reason for returning the money?
options: It was generosity on his part
He was afraid of getting caught
It was simply what honesty required of him
quiz.explanation: He told the tourist that returning it wasn't generosity, it was simply what honesty required of him that night.

quiz.question: Why is the tourist vulnerable to a payment mistake?
options: He is tired and unfamiliar with the currency
quiz.explanation: The setting explains the accidental overpayment.

quiz.question: What makes keeping the first extra amount dishonest?
options: The tourist gave it by mistake while trusting the driver to calculate
quiz.explanation: Consent to the correct fare is not consent to four times the fare.

quiz.question: How does the narrator prevent a similar problem?
options: He counts money in front of passengers and shows the fare clearly
quiz.explanation: The revised ending turns integrity into a better process.

quiz.question: If the tourist offers a tip after understanding the fare, what changes?
options: The tourist loses the right to choose
It is now a separate informed choice that can be accepted or declined
quiz.explanation: The script separates mistake from voluntary generosity.

quiz.question: What is the strongest evidence of the driver’s intention?
options: He returns when tired and explains the exact difference
quiz.explanation: Costly corrective action supports the claim of honesty.
